coding_method: Assistant review of complete 4,797-character rendered answer, four scoped exact DOM hrefs and existing browser snapshots/activity. No external webpage visits, research verification or independent human double-coding.
coding_scope: Substantively named tools/services/surfaces; supplied targets remain separate. Supporting citation-label brands are not converted into substantive tool mentions or resource recommendations.

answer_type.rationale: Seven sections prioritize methodology, replication, per-engine results, prompt bias, noise, supporting signals and provenance; no specific visibility-checker product is suggested.

branded_and_unbranded_buyer_prompts.evidence: buyer-intent, unbranded queries are far more meaningful than “what is [your brand]?”

repeated_runs.evidence: Note whether the tool accounts for stochasticity with repeated queries.

fresh_sessions.evidence: Run them in fresh ChatGPT and Grok sessions (new chats, memory cleared if possible, web search enabled).

model_search_version_logging.evidence: Engines, models, and whether web search was on

citations_mentions_recommendations_disti.evidence: Mentions without citations or positive recommendations have limited value.

citation_and_mention_rates_separate.evidence: Citation rate — does it link to your site or pages?

citation_and_mention_observations_separa.evidence: Was your product named? In what position / prominence? Was your site cited?

raw_answer_inspection.evidence: Can you access raw answers or at least screenshots of key prompts?

numerator_denominator_definition.evidence: simple mention rate (answers naming you ÷ total answers)

composite_score_weighting_disclosed_or_c.evidence: Formula: simple mention rate (answers naming you ÷ total answers), position-weighted, sentiment-adjusted, or something else?

composite_score_caution.evidence: Always look at engine-level numbers, not just a composite.

uncertainty_variance.evidence: Day-to-day and run-to-run variance is normal. Look for trends over weeks, not single scores.

human_checking.evidence: Replicate it yourself (the highest-ROI check for a bootstrapped builder)

downstream_traffic_or_impressions.evidence: Actual AI referral traffic in your analytics (GA4 or similar)

entity_observations.evidence: Focus next on the inputs that actually influence answers: clear entity presence, authoritative third-party mentions (reviews, docs, comparison content, communities), and (especially for Grok) relevant X activity.
entity_observations.notes: Advises relevant X activity as a content/community input, not a dedicated visibility-measurement tool. Claims of influence are unverified model output.

entity_observations.evidence: one brand could score high on Claude/Grok while being nearly invisible on ChatGPT.
entity_observations.notes: Benchmark context only, not a suggestion to use Claude.

notes: Activity contains a grouped two-search control, a separately displayed web query with 10 results, and three browsed-link controls. Exact query coverage is partial.
The 35-hit source badge is not a unique citation count.
Workspace-explored activity labels do not establish the underlying contents or their influence.
Benchmark overlap, near-14-point weather effects, brand-score differences, model/engine behavior and reliability claims remain unverified platform output.
capture_scope.public_copy_note: Body length and source hash describe this redacted public record. Original citation position indexes are omitted; semantic judgments are retained.

coding_cautions: GA4 is an analytics example and X is content/community advice; neither is a named visibility-scoring checker here.
The answer explicitly distinguishes mentions, citations and positive recommendations, but does not define a separate recommendation-rate formula.
The four cited publishers are not substantively recommended merely because their citation labels are rendered in the answer.
Avoid treating model-generated numerical claims as findings independently established by this experiment.
